raw_response:
*Sitting on the stoop, thinking about the year ahead...*

Aiyo, 74 years now, been working these 5 mu since before my boy was born. My old man's gone ten years, my son and his wife work in the factory in town, only come back for the busy times — wheat harvest and maize planting. My grandson's in school. So mostly it's just me out there, slow but I manage.

Same as every year, really. Wheat goes in after the maize comes off in October, around when the Cold Dew comes. Maize goes in right after wheat's cut in June — no time to rest, you gotta get it in the ground before it gets too hot.

I buy fertilizer at the供销社 in town. One bag of 复合肥 is about one mu's worth for the base, then a bag of 尿素 covers a couple mu for the topdressing. I don't use as much as some — can't afford to waste it, and my land's been good to me, doesn't need so much. Seed I buy fresh every year for the maize — the hybrid kind, everyone uses it now, my nephew picks it up for me. Wheat seed sometimes I save a little from last year, sometimes buy.

Water — well's close by, but pumping costs. Wheat needs the winter water and then one more when it's greening up in spring. Maize, if it rains good in July I don't water at all. If dry, once at tasseling time.

Pests — I spray the weeds once for each crop, that's it usually. My eyes aren't so good anymore but you can see if the bugs are bad.

My son rents the rototiller from 老王 next door when he comes home — 40 块 a mu, done in an afternoon.

Last year wheat gave me about 400 kg a mu, maize a bit better, maybe 450. Nothing special but enough. I sell what I don't eat, keeps me going.
